Irene,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. For the upcoming SIG and SOC2 evidence package we need a consolidated deliverable that covers your vulnerability management posture with a specific focus on credentialed (authenticated) dynamic scanning and production patch windows. Our auditors are asking for:

- Proof of weekly authenticated DAST runs (or cadence you run) against production-staged endpoints and evidence that findings are triaged into your tracking system.
- A mapping of CVSS tiers to your remediation SLA (critical/high/medium) and typical closure timelines for prod vs non-prod.
- A short sample of proof-of-fix for one recent CVE (logs or ticket + before/after scan snippet).
- Exported scan artifacts (hashes/manifest), a manifest of patch windows, and any exceptions/compensating controls.

Can you provide a single archive or link with the above, and preferable CSV/CSV+pdf proof for auditors? If you need a template for how they'd like it structured we can share ours.

Raj / Irene / team — looping in exact operating bullets so auditors get a single-source answer. Attaching the three requested artifacts with this message. Highlights below; full detail is in the attached manifest and the Drive folder linked above.

Summary of VM controls & cadence (credentialed DAST focus):
- Credentialed dynamic scans: weekly targeted credentialed DAST against production-staged endpoints (every Wed 02:00–05:00 PT). Scans run with service-account credentials; test accounts have MFA bypass tokens limited to scanning timeframe.
- Full fleet DAST (unauthenticated + authenticated sweep): monthly on the dedicated scanning fleet (first Sunday of month).
- Nightly SCA / dependency scanning for repos (incremental).
- Passive monitoring & WAF-assisted discovery runs continuously; findings are triaged to reduce false positives.

Ticketing & evidence flow:
- Every confirmed finding generates a Jira ticket (see JIRA-3241 as an example). Tickets include raw scanner output, trimmed payloads, and a SHA256 manifest that we include in evidence bundles.
- For CVE proof-of-fix we attach: pre-scan snippet, ticket with remediation details, deploy job id (CI/CD), and post-scan snippet showing the artifact no longer triggers.

Remediation SLAs (prod-targeted):
- Critical (CVSS >= 9.0 or active exploit): response within 24 hours, mitigation or hotfix within 7 calendar days.
- High (7.0–8.9): acknowledge and schedule within 3 business days; remediated within 30 calendar days.
- Medium (4.0–6.9): track and resolve within 90 calendar days unless elevated via risk review.

Compensating controls & exceptions:
- Exceptions go through a documented risk acceptance workflow with a compensating control checklist (WAF rule, network microsegmentation, additional logging). Exception records are included in the bundle.

Operational notes (audit-friendly):
- All scans are signed (artifact manifest) and stored in an immutable bucket with 365-day retention for SOC2 evidence.
- We keep a rolling 12-week credentialed-scan history in CSV for quick auditor access; full raw outputs are archived for 24 months.

Attachments included: credentialed-dast-scan-summary-202704.zip (contains CSVs + manifest), patch-window-log-202704.csv, cve-closure-manifest-2027Q2.pdf

Inline sample (redacted) — pre/post scan snippet:
> Pre-scan (2027-03-28 02:03:14): /api/v1/auth responded 401, vuln id: CVE-2026-1234, payload -> sql_injection_vector
> Post-deploy (2027-04-02 03:12:09): /api/v1/auth responded 200, scan test vector did not trigger; ticket JIRA-3241 marked resolved, deployment id: deploy-20270402-57b3

If you'd like, we can prepare a short one-page control mapping specifically for SIG (control IDs + evidence file names).

Ben Carter
Head of Security Engineering (VM & Scanning)
